# `Q-2-52` — Shortcode delimiter not separated by a space

> A shortcode's delimiters must be separated from its content by
> whitespace. Write `{{{< fa plus >}}}` — a space after `{{<` and a
> space before `>}}` — rather than \{\{\<fa plus\>\}\}.

## What this means

A shortcode is written `{{{< name arg1 arg2 >}}}`, and the space on each
side of the content is part of the syntax rather than a matter of
style. Both of these are errors:

- \{\{\<fa plus \>\}\} — no space after the opening delimiter.
- \{\{\< fa plus\>\}\} — no space before the closing one.

Quarto 1 accepted them. It matched shortcodes with a regular
expression, which tolerated the tight spelling incidentally. Quarto 2
parses shortcodes as part of the document grammar, and requires the
separator so that `{{` at the start of a word stays unambiguous — `{{`
is also the opening delimiter of Jinja, Handlebars, Liquid and several
other template languages that Quarto documents routinely quote.

## Why this happens

- **A document ported from Quarto 1.** This is by far the most common
  cause. The tight spelling renders fine under Quarto 1, so it
  accumulates in a project unnoticed.
- **Only one delimiter was fixed.** Adding the space after `{{<` but
  not before `>}}` leaves the shortcode just as unparseable. Both
  delimiters need it.
- **The escaped spelling.** `{{{{< ... >}}}}`, which shows a shortcode
  literally instead of running it, takes the separator on the same
  terms.

## How to fix

Put a space on both sides of the shortcode's content:

```markdown
Click the {{{< fa plus >}}} icon.
```

To convert a whole file or a whole project, `qmd-syntax-helper` will do
it for you:

```bash
qmd-syntax-helper convert -r q-2-52 -i path/to/document.qmd
```

The rule rewrites both delimiters, and reports each one it changed. The
spaced form is what Quarto 1 emits and both versions accept, so a
converted document still builds under Quarto 1.

## Example

A line written tight, \{\{\<fa plus\>\}\}, becomes:

```markdown
Click the {{{< fa plus >}}} icon.
```

## Related errors

- [`Q-2-34`](Q-2-34.qmd) — an unquoted shortcode parameter that starts
  with a digit. A closing delimiter written tight after such a value
  produces this error, `Q-2-52`, rather than `Q-2-34`: the value is
  fine and the space is what is missing.
- [`Q-2-27`](Q-2-27.qmd) — a shortcode that is never closed.
